words.en: To monopolise means to have or take the greatest share or control of something, especially in a way that prevents others from having or using it.

words.ex: The committee gave their approbations to the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 委员会对新政策给予了批准。
words.en: Approval or praise, especially when given formally or officially.

words.tr: adj. 系统的；有组织的；有条理的
words.ex: He follows a systematical plan to study every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天遵循一个系统的计划学习。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of a system; methodical.

words.ex: The new policy was viewed unfavourably by the majority of employees.
words.ex_cn: 大多数员工对新政策持不赞成态度。
words.en: In a way that is not favorable; with disapproval or disadvantage.

words.ex: The public expressed condemnation for the violent act.
words.ex_cn: 公众对这一暴力行为表示谴责。
words.en: Condemnation is the act of saying that something or someone is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: He circumvented the security system by using a back door.
words.ex_cn: 他通过使用后门绕过了安全系统。
words.en: To find a way around an obstacle or restriction, often by cleverness or deceit.

words.ex: The terms mentioned hereinbefore are crucial for understanding the contract.
words.ex_cn: 在上文中提到的条款对于理解合同至关重要。
words.en: In the preceding part of this document or text.

words.ex: The fractions have different denominators.
words.ex_cn: 这些分数有不同的分母。
words.en: In mathematics, the denominator is the bottom number in a fraction that shows into how many equal parts the whole is divided.

words.tr: v. 恶化，变坏( deteriorate的过去式和过去分词 )
words.ex: The road deteriorated after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨之后，这条路状况恶化了。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.tr: v. 预先假定；以…为先决条件
words.ex: Presupposing that the meeting will go as planned, we can start preparing the documents.
words.ex_cn: v. 预先假定会议将按计划进行，我们可以开始准备文件。
words.en: If you presuppose that something is true, you assume it is true without knowing for certain that it is.

words.tr: n. 意外发生；附加事件
words.ex: The supervention of a storm delayed our flight.
words.ex_cn: n. 一场风暴的意外发生延误了我们的航班。
words.en: The occurrence of something, especially something unexpected or additional.

words.ex: He gave an anticipatory smile before the surprise.
words.ex_cn: 他在惊喜到来前露出了预期的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as anticipatory, you mean that it is characterized by anticipation. It involves expecting or looking forward to something with a feeling of excitement or anxiety.

words.ex: He is a propagandist who spreads false news.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个散布虚假新闻的宣传者。
words.en: A propagandist is someone who spreads propaganda, which is information, especially of a biased or misleading nature, used to promote a political cause or point of view.

words.ex: The logo is recognizable even from far away.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志即使从远处也能辨认出来。
words.en: Able to be recognized or identified from previous encounters or knowledge.

words.tr: n. 重商主义者; adj. 重商主义的
words.ex: The mercantilist believed that gold made a nation strong.
words.ex_cn: 这位重商主义者认为黄金使国家强大。
words.en: A mercantilist is someone who believes in or supports mercantilism, an economic theory that advocates government regulation of a nation's economy for the purpose of augmenting state power at the expense of rival national powers.

words.ex: He spends too much time worrying about trivialities.
words.ex_cn: 他花了太多时间担心琐事。
words.en: Trivialities are small, unimportant details or things that are not worth serious attention.

words.ex: I congratulate you on your success.
words.ex_cn: 我祝贺你取得成功。
words.en: If you congratulate someone, you express pleasure for something good that has happened to them, or you praise them for something they have achieved.

words.tr: n. 谈判；磋商；谈判（negotiation 的复数）；
words.ex: The two countries started negotiations to end the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家开始了谈判以结束冲突。
words.en: Discussions between people who have different aims or intentions, during which they try to reach an agreement.

words.ex: He was charged with manslaughter after the car accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在车祸后被指控过失杀人。
words.en: Manslaughter is the crime of killing a person when the killer did not intend to do it or cannot be responsible for their actions at the time.

words.ex: We had a short conversation about the weather.
words.ex_cn: 我们简短地聊了聊天气。
words.en: A conversation is a talk between two or more people, in which news and ideas are exchanged.

words.ex: The contrivances in the novel were both ingenious and complex.
words.ex_cn: 小说中的设计既巧妙又复杂。
words.en: Contrivances are clever devices or schemes, often used to achieve a particular purpose, sometimes in a way that is artificial or forced.

words.tr: adj. 官僚的；官僚主义的；
words.ex: The bureaucratic process made it hard to get a permit.
words.ex_cn: 官僚程序让申请许可证变得困难。
words.en: If you describe a system, organization, or process as bureaucratic, you mean that it is complicated and inefficient because of a large number of rules and procedures.

words.ex: The child suffered maltreatment from his caregiver.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子受到了照顾者的虐待。
words.en: Maltreatment is cruel or violent treatment of someone.

words.tr: adj. 不满意的；不高兴的； v. “dissatisfy”的过去式；
words.ex: He was dissatisfied with the service.
words.ex_cn: 他对服务不满意。
words.en: If you are dissatisfied with something, you are not contented or pleased with it.

words.tr: adj. 可认识的；可辨别的；可公认的；
words.ex: The logo is recognisable even from far away.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志即使从远处也能认出来。
words.en: If something is recognisable, it is easy to know what it is or who it is because you have seen, heard, or experienced it before.

words.ex: She superintends the entire project to ensure everything runs smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 她监督整个项目，确保一切顺利进行。
words.en: To be in charge of something and make sure that it is done properly.

words.ex: The room is well proportioned, with high ceilings and large windows.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间比例很好，有高高的天花板和大窗户。
words.en: Having the correct or appropriate relationship in size, amount, or degree between different parts.

words.ex: His idiosyncrasy is talking to himself while reading.
words.ex_cn: 他的怪癖是读书时自言自语。
words.en: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar or unusual habit, way of behaving, or feature that someone or something has.

words.ex: He definitively refused to join the project.
words.ex_cn: 他明确地拒绝了加入这个项目。
words.en: In a manner that is conclusive and not subject to further dispute or revision.

words.ex: Her insinuations about his honesty made him very uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 她对他诚实的暗示让他感到非常不舒服。
words.en: Insinuations are indirect suggestions or hints, often implying something negative or unpleasant.

words.tr: v. 过度地生产( overproduce的过去式和过去分词 )
words.ex: The movie was criticized for being overproduced.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因过度制作而受到批评。
words.en: To produce more of something than is needed or wanted.

words.ex: The measurements of the room were taken by the builder.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工人测量了房间的尺寸。
words.en: Measurements refer to the size, length, or amount of something, as established by measuring.

words.ex: She spent the morning replenishing the shelves with new products.
words.ex_cn: 她花了一上午时间用新产品补充货架。
words.en: To replenish something means to make it full or complete again by replacing what has been used or lost.

words.ex: The news was disseminated quickly through the internet.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻通过互联网迅速传播开来。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or give out something, especially news, information, ideas, etc., to a lot of people.

words.tr: v. 使外部化；使客观化
words.ex: The company externalised its customer service department to reduce costs.
words.ex_cn: v. 公司将客户服务部门外包以降低成本。
words.en: To make something external or to express something outwardly.

words.ex: The polarisation of society into rich and poor is becoming more pronounced.
words.ex_cn: 社会贫富两极分化变得越来越明显。
words.en: Polarisation refers to the process or state of dividing or causing to divide into two sharply contrasting groups or sets of opinions or beliefs.

words.tr: n. 不准确，误差( inaccuracy的名词复数 ); 不准确的说法
words.ex: The report has some inaccuracies.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告有一些不准确的地方。
words.en: Inaccuracies refer to mistakes or errors in information, data, or details.

words.tr: n. 江湖医术；骗子行为
words.ex: His charlatanism was exposed when his fake cures failed to work.
words.ex_cn: 他的江湖医术在他的假药无效时被揭露了。
words.en: Charlatanism refers to the practice or methods of a charlatan, especially the fraudulent or deceptive practices in medicine or other fields.

words.ex: She is generalising her findings from a small sample to the entire population.
words.ex_cn: 她正在将从小样本中得出的结论推广到整个人群。
words.en: To make a general or broad statement by inferring from specific cases.

words.tr: n. 时代错误；不合时代的人或事物
words.ex: The film was criticized for its anachronisms, such as a modern car in a medieval setting.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因其时代错误而受到批评，比如在中世纪背景中出现了一辆现代汽车。
words.en: An anachronism is something that is out of its proper time in history, especially something that belongs to an earlier time.

words.ex: The bomb was capable of obliterating the entire city.
words.ex_cn: 这颗炸弹能够彻底毁灭整个城市。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove it completely so that it no longer exists.

words.ex: You can pay conveniently online.
words.ex_cn: 你可以方便地在线支付。
words.en: In a way that is suitable for one's needs or purposes; in a way that is easy to use or access.

words.ex: The disease and its concomitants were studied extensively.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病及其伴随情况被广泛研究。
words.en: Concomitants are things that naturally accompany or are associated with something else.

words.tr: v. 深思，细想，仔细考虑( contemplate的过去式 ); 注视，凝视; 考虑接受（发生某事
words.ex: He contemplated quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他考虑过辞掉工作。
words.en: Considered or thought about carefully, often before a decision is made.

words.ex: The store discontinued the old model.
words.ex_cn: 商店停止销售旧型号。
words.en: No longer produced or provided; stopped.

words.tr: adj. 超越的；杰出的；卓越的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was transcendent.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是超凡的。
words.en: If you describe something as transcendent, you mean that it is extremely good or impressive, often in a way that goes beyond the ordinary.

words.tr: adj. 无原则的；无道德的；
words.ex: He is an unprincipled man who lies for money.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个为了钱就撒谎的无原则的人。
words.en: If you describe a person or their actions as unprincipled, you are criticizing them for their lack of moral principles and because they do things which are wrong or dishonest.

words.tr:
adj. 包含的；围绕的
v. 包含；围绕；“encompass”的现在分词
words.ex: The plan is encompassing all the students in the class.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划涵盖了班级里的所有学生。
words.en: To include or contain something as a part of a whole.

words.ex: The chemist developed new formulations for the medication.
words.ex_cn: 化学家为药物开发了新的配方。
words.en: The act or process of creating or preparing something, especially a product or a plan, in a systematic way.

words.ex: The rock is carbonaceous and black.
words.ex_cn: 这块岩石是含碳的，呈黑色。
words.en: Containing carbon or coal.

words.ex: The government is trying to reduce the consumptions of natural resources.
words.ex_cn: 政府正在努力减少自然资源的消耗。
words.en: The act of using up resources or goods, or the amount used.

words.tr: n. 教条主义者；空谈理论的人
words.ex: The doctrinaires insisted on following the theory without considering practical implications.
words.ex_cn: 教条主义者坚持遵循理论而不考虑实际影响。
words.en: A person who applies doctrine in a rigid and inflexible manner, often without considering practical circumstances.

words.tr: adj. 有启迪作用的； v. “enlighten”的现在分词；
words.ex: The talk was enlightening and helped me understand life better.
words.ex_cn: 这场演讲很有启发性，帮助我更好地理解了人生。
words.en: Providing insight, understanding, or knowledge.

words.tr: n. 源头; 根源; 源地
words.ex: The university is the fountainhead of new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学是新思想的源头。
words.en: The fountainhead is the origin or source of something, especially a stream or river. It can also refer to the primary source of an idea, movement, or activity.

words.ex: The Ten Commandments are fundamental to many religious teachings.
words.ex_cn: 十诫是许多宗教教义的基础。
words.en: A commandment is an authoritative order or instruction, especially one of the Ten Commandments in the Bible.

words.ex: She is endeavouring to complete the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 她正在努力按时完成项目。
words.en: To try hard to do or achieve something.

words.ex: The celebrity's endorsements have significantly boosted the brand's sales.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人的支持显著提升了该品牌的销售额。
words.en: An endorsement is a statement or action which shows that you support or approve of something or someone.

words.ex: He is specialising in computer science.
words.ex_cn: 他正在专攻计算机科学。
words.en: To concentrate on and become expert in a particular subject or skill.

words.ex: The town is famous for its distilleries that produce high-quality whiskey.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇以其生产高品质威士忌的蒸馏厂而闻名。
words.en: A distillery is a place where spirits such as whiskey, gin, or vodka are produced by the process of distillation.

words.tr: adj. 致死的；有害的；传染的
words.ex: The pestilential conditions in the refugee camp led to a rapid spread of disease.
words.ex_cn: 难民营中引起瘟疫的条件导致了疾病的迅速传播。
words.en: Pestilential is used to describe something that is harmful or destructive, especially in a way that is difficult to control or stop.

words.ex: The king has special prerogatives that others do not have.
words.ex_cn: 国王有一些别人没有的特权。
words.en: A prerogative is a right or privilege exclusive to a particular individual or class.

words.ex: He faced public denunciation for his lies.
words.ex_cn: 他因撒谎而遭到公众的谴责。
words.en: Denunciation is the act of criticizing something or someone strongly and publicly.

words.ex: Spendthrifts often waste money on things they do not need.
words.ex_cn: 挥霍者常常把钱浪费在他们不需要的东西上。
words.en: A spendthrift is someone who spends money in an extravagant, irresponsible way.

words.ex: The model approximates the behavior of the real system.
words.ex_cn: 这个模型近似地模拟了真实系统的行为。
words.en: To come close to; to be similar to something in quality, nature, or quantity.

words.ex: The coach unmercifully pushed the team to their limits.
words.ex_cn: 教练无情地将团队推到了极限。
words.en: In a way that shows no mercy or pity; cruelly.

words.ex: The company is centralizing its operations to improve efficiency.
words.ex_cn: v. 公司正在集中其运营以提高效率。
words.en: To bring under central control; to concentrate (authority, power, etc.) in a central organization or place.

words.tr: v. 使突然发生；加速；沉淀
words.ex: The sudden storm precipitates a flood in the valley.
words.ex_cn: 突如其来的暴雨加速了山谷中的洪水。
words.en: To cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly; to cause a substance to be deposited in solid form from a solution.

words.ex: He works in horticulture at a local garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在当地的一个花园从事园艺工作。
words.en: Horticulture is the study and practice of growing and cultivating plants, especially flowers, fruits, and vegetables.

words.ex: The installation of the new machine took two days.
words.ex_cn: 新机器的安置花了两天时间。
words.en: The act of installing or the state of being installed.

words.ex: The sharecropper worked hard to cultivate the land but received only a small portion of the crop.
words.ex_cn: 这位收益分成的佃农辛勤耕种土地，但只能得到收成的一小部分。
words.en: A sharecropper is a tenant farmer who pays as rent a share of the crop.

words.tr: adj. 每五年一次的；持续五年的
words.ex: The company holds a quinquennial review of its policies.
words.ex_cn: 公司每五年对其政策进行一次审查。
words.en: Happening every five years or lasting for five years.

words.ex: School is recommencing after the holiday break.
words.ex_cn: 假期结束后学校重新开学。
words.en: To begin again or resume something that was previously started.

words.ex: The government's suppressions of the protests led to widespread unrest.
words.ex_cn: 政府对抗议活动的镇压导致了广泛的不安。
words.en: The act of ending something by force or the act of preventing something from being expressed or known.

words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: Prostitution is the practice or occupation of engaging in sexual activity with someone for payment.

words.ex: He worked relentlessly to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他不懈地工作以完成这个项目。
words.en: In a way that is harsh, inflexible, or unyielding; without stopping or becoming less severe.

words.tr: n. 管理者的职位；董事（或经理）职位、任期
words.ex: He accepted the directorship of the company.
words.ex_cn: 他接受了公司的董事职位。
words.en: The position or term of office of a director.

words.tr: adj. 声名狼藉的；名誉不好的
words.ex: He works for a disreputable company.
words.ex_cn: 他为一家声誉不佳的公司工作。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is disreputable, you mean that they have a bad reputation because they are connected with activities that are not considered respectable.

words.ex: He studies architecture at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学学习建筑学。
words.en: Architecture is the art and science of designing buildings and other physical structures.

words.tr: adv. 无限地；广大无边地；不能测量地
words.ex: Her contribution to the project has improved it immeasurably.
words.ex_cn: 她对项目的贡献极大地改进了它。
words.en: To an extent that cannot be measured; infinitely.

words.ex: Some people believe that we have many lives in different incarnations.
words.ex_cn: 有些人相信我们在不同的化身中有多次生命。
words.en: The embodiment or manifestation of a deity, spirit, or abstract quality in human or animal form.

words.tr: n. 慈善；博爱；慈善事业
words.ex: He gives money to charity because of his philanthropy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为慈善精神而捐钱给慈善机构。
words.en: Philanthropy is the act of donating money, goods, time, or effort to support a charitable cause, usually over an extended period of time and in regard to a defined objective.

words.ex: She rediscovered her love for painting after many years.
words.ex_cn: 她多年后重新发现了对绘画的热爱。
words.en: To discover something again, especially something that had been forgotten or lost.

words.ex: The idea is conceptually simple but practically challenging.
words.ex_cn: 这个想法在概念上很简单，但在实践中却颇具挑战性。
words.en: In a way that relates to or involves the mental concept of something.

words.ex: The government adopted several expediencies to address the crisis.
words.ex_cn: 政府采取了多项权宜之计来应对危机。
words.en: Expediencies are actions or measures that are convenient and practical, especially in a particular situation, but may not be morally correct or the best in the long term.

words.ex: The conference hired professional interpreters to facilitate communication between the international delegates.
words.ex_cn: 会议聘请了专业口译员以促进国际代表之间的交流。
words.en: Interpreters are people who translate spoken words from one language to another, especially as a profession.

words.ex: The ancient Egyptians believed in the imperishable soul.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人相信灵魂是不朽的。
words.en: If you describe something as imperishable, you mean that it cannot disappear or be destroyed.

words.tr: v. 释义，意译( paraphrase的现在分词 )
words.ex: He is paraphrasing the paragraph to make it simpler.
words.ex_cn: 他正在改写这段话，使其更简单。
words.en: Paraphrasing involves rewording or rephrasing text or speech in order to achieve greater clarity, often to simplify or clarify the original content without changing its meaning.

words.ex: Silviculture is essential for sustainable forest management.
words.ex_cn: 造林学对于可持续森林管理至关重要。
words.en: Silviculture is the practice of controlling the establishment, growth, composition, health, and quality of forests to meet diverse needs and values.

words.ex: He remonstrates when the teacher gives too much homework.
words.ex_cn: 当老师布置太多作业时，他提出抗议。
words.en: To remonstrate means to make a forcefully reproachful protest or to argue in protest or opposition.

words.tr: v. 证明，证实；使具体化（substantiate 的过去式和过去分词）
words.ex: His claim was substantiated by the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的说法得到了证据的支持。
words.en: To substantiate something means to provide evidence to support or prove the truth of it.

words.ex: The revolutionist was determined to overthrow the government.
words.ex_cn: 这位革命者决心推翻政府。
words.en: A revolutionist is someone who tries to cause a revolution or who takes an active part in one.

words.ex: The company reported significant depreciations in its assets this quarter.
words.ex_cn: 该公司报告本季度资产大幅贬值。
words.en: A reduction in the value of an asset over time, due in particular to wear and tear.

words.ex: Fertilisation happens when the sperm meets the egg.
words.ex_cn: 当精子与卵子相遇时，受精就发生了。
words.en: The process of union between a sperm and an egg to form a new organism.

words.ex: The obstetricians at the hospital are highly skilled in managing high-risk pregnancies.
words.ex_cn: 医院里的产科医生在管理高风险妊娠方面非常熟练。
words.en: A doctor who specializes in childbirth and the care of women giving birth.

words.ex: It is inconceivable that he forgot his own birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他忘了自己生日，这简直难以想象。
words.en: If something is inconceivable, it is impossible to imagine or believe because it is so unlikely.

words.ex: The process of crystallising sugar requires precise temperature control.
words.ex_cn: v. 结晶糖的过程需要精确的温度控制。
words.en: To cause to form crystals or to become clear and definite in form.

words.ex: The country is undergoing modernisation to improve its cities.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在经历现代化，以改善其城市。
words.en: The process of making something modern or more suitable for the present time.

words.ex: He will go out conditionally if he finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 如果他完成作业，他才会出去。
words.en: In a way that depends on certain conditions or requirements being met.

words.tr: v. 重建； adj. 重建的，改造的 v. 重建( reconstruct的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: The old house was reconstructed last year.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子去年被重建了。
words.en: If something is reconstructed, it is built again after it has been damaged or destroyed.

words.tr: adj. 令人失望的；令人扫兴的； v. “disappoint”的现在分词；
words.ex: The movie was disappointing.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影令人失望。
words.en: If something is disappointing, it is not as good as you hoped it would be.

words.tr: adv. 成几何级数地；几何图形地
words.ex: The shapes are arranged geometrically.
words.ex_cn: 这些形状是按几何方式排列的。
words.en: In a way that relates to geometry or the methods of geometry.

words.tr: adv. 追溯地,有追溯效力地
words.ex: The law changed the rules retroactively.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律追溯性地更改了规则。
words.en: If a decision or action is retroactive, it is intended to take effect from a date in the past.

words.ex: He asked for reimbursement for his travel costs.
words.ex_cn: 他要求报销旅行费用。
words.en: The act of compensating someone for an expense or loss incurred.

words.ex: The signification of this word is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这个词的含义是清楚的。
words.en: The meaning or importance of something.

words.ex: The administrator fixed the computer system.
words.ex_cn: 管理人员修复了计算机系统。
words.en: An administrator is a person whose job involves helping to organize and supervise the way that an organization or institution functions.

words.ex: The stabilization of the economy took many years.
words.ex_cn: 经济的稳定花了许多年。
words.en: The process of making something physically stable or the act of stabilizing the economy or a patient's condition.

words.tr: n. 贸易保护主义；保护（贸易）主义
words.ex: The government uses protectionism to help local factories.
words.ex_cn: 政府使用保护主义来帮助本地工厂。
words.en: Protectionism is the policy of protecting domestic industries from foreign competition by taxing imports.

words.ex: He packed his paraphernalia before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 他在旅行前收拾好了随身用具。
words.en: The equipment, apparatus, or furnishing used in or necessary for a particular activity.

words.ex: He is inexperienced in managing teams.
words.ex_cn: 他在管理团队方面没有经验。
words.en: If you describe someone as inexperienced, you mean that they have little knowledge or experience of a particular situation or activity.

words.tr: n. 安装；装置；就职；军事设施；装置( installation的名词复数 )；
words.ex: The installations of the new pipes took two days.
words.ex_cn: 新管道的安装花了两天时间。
words.en: the act of installing something; something that is installed, especially a piece of equipment or a work of art

words.ex: Wearing shorts to the meeting is inappropriate.
words.ex_cn: 穿短裤去参加会议是不合适的。
words.en: If you say that something is inappropriate, you are criticizing it because you think it is not suitable for a particular situation or purpose.

words.ex: The soda shows effervescence when poured.
words.ex_cn: 汽水倒出来时会冒泡。
words.en: Effervescence is the process of bubbles forming in a liquid, which is often associated with the release of gas. It can also describe a lively and enthusiastic quality in a person or atmosphere.

words.tr: v. 进行哲学思考；探讨哲学问题
words.ex: He often philosophises about the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 他经常探讨生命的意义。
words.en: To engage in or discuss philosophical questions or theories.

words.ex: Her reminiscences of childhood were filled with joy and laughter.
words.ex_cn: 她对童年的回忆充满了欢乐和笑声。
words.en: Recollections of past events or experiences, often shared in a nostalgic manner.

words.tr: n. 争论；论据；论证；论点
words.ex: His argumentation lasted for hours.
words.ex_cn: 他的争论持续了数小时。
words.en: Argumentation is the process of reasoning systematically in support of an idea, action, or theory.

words.tr: v. 限制；约束；画外接圆
words.ex: The law circumscribes the powers of the government.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了政府的权力。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit or restrict it, or to draw a line around it.

words.tr: adj. 难以形容的；无法描述的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was indescribable.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美无法形容。
words.en: If you describe something as indescribable, you mean that it is so extreme, unusual, or shocking that you cannot describe it.

words.ex: He felt psychological stress before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到心理压力。
words.en: Relating to the mental and emotional state of a person.

words.ex: The dissemination of information helps people learn.
words.ex_cn: 信息的传播帮助人们学习。
words.en: The act of spreading something, especially information, widely.

words.ex: He overestimated his ability to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他高估了自己按时完成项目的能力。
words.en: To estimate something to be greater or more important than it really is.

words.ex: The rectification of the error took only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误的纠正只花了一天时间。
words.en: Rectification refers to the act of correcting something that is wrong or the process of converting alternating current to direct current in electrical engineering.

words.ex: The artist embraced the imperfections in her pottery, seeing them as signs of its handmade quality.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家接受了她陶器中的不完美，将它们视为手工制作的标志。
words.en: Imperfections refer to faults, flaws, or undesirable features in something or someone.

words.ex: The singer sang with piano accompaniment.
words.ex_cn: 歌手在钢琴伴奏下演唱。
words.en: An accompaniment is a musical part which supports or partners a solo instrument, voice, or group.

words.tr: adj. 不确定的；不明确的
words.ex: The result is indeterminate.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不确定的。
words.en: If something is indeterminate, you cannot say exactly what it is.

words.tr: n. 深思熟虑；审议；商议
words.ex: The jury's deliberations lasted for three days.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团的审议持续了三天。
words.en: Deliberations refer to careful consideration or discussion of a subject, often before making a decision.

words.tr: n. 结果，后果( ramification的名词复数 )
words.ex: The decision has serious ramifications.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定有严重的后果。
words.en: The ramifications of an action, event, or decision are the complex or complicated results that follow from it.

words.tr: adj. 不勉强的；非强迫的；不受约束的
words.ex: The boy ran unconstrained through the field.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在田野里无拘无束地奔跑。
words.en: If someone is unconstrained, they are free to act as they wish without being restricted by anything.

words.ex: He loves studying jurisprudence to understand laws better.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢学习法学以更好地理解法律。
words.en: Jurisprudence is the study of law and the principles on which law is based.

words.ex: The amplifier gives amplification to the sound.
words.ex_cn: 放大器对声音进行放大。
words.en: The process of increasing the volume, extent, or significance of something.

words.tr: v. 预先决定；预先确定
words.ex: The program predetermines the order of the questions.
words.ex_cn: 这个程序预先确定了问题的顺序。
words.en: To decide or establish something in advance.

words.tr: adv. 陡然地；急剧地；草率地
words.ex: The road descends precipitously towards the valley.
words.ex_cn: 道路陡峭地向山谷下降。
words.en: In a way that is dangerously high or steep; done without careful consideration.

words.tr: n. 不同，相异点，相异; 差
words.ex: There is a big dissimilarity between the two pictures.
words.ex_cn: 这两张图片之间有很大的不同。
words.en: The state or quality of being dissimilar; difference.

words.tr: v. 描述…的特性；成为…的特征
words.ex: The novel characterizes the hero as a man of integrity.
words.ex_cn: v. 这部小说将主人公描绘为一个正直的人。
words.en: To describe the qualities or features of something or someone; to be a typical feature of something.

words.ex: The guests were ceremoniously welcomed at the palace gates.
words.ex_cn: 客人们在宫殿大门受到了隆重的欢迎。
words.en: In a manner that is marked by ceremony or formality.

words.ex: She was inexpressibly happy when she saw her son after ten years.
words.ex_cn: adv. 当她十年后见到儿子时，她无法表达地高兴。
words.en: In a way that cannot be expressed or described in words.

words.ex: They have conversations every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天晚上都有对话。
words.en: Conversations are informal talks between two or more people in which news and ideas are exchanged.

words.ex: The incongruities in his story made it hard to believe.
words.ex_cn: 他故事中的不一致之处让人难以相信。
words.en: Incongruities refer to things that are out of place or inconsistent with their surroundings or context.

words.tr: n. 长子身份；长子继承权
words.ex: In many historical societies, primogeniture dictated that the eldest son would inherit the family estate.
words.ex_cn: 在许多历史社会中，长子继承权规定长子将继承家族的地产。
words.en: The system by which the eldest son in a family inherits all his parents' property.

words.tr: adj. 分散的；去中心化的
words.ex: The company has a decentralised management structure.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有一个分散的管理结构。
words.en: Decentralised means that control or decision-making is distributed away from a central authority or location.

words.ex: The map shows topographical details of the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图显示了山脉的地形细节。
words.en: Relating to the arrangement of the physical features of an area.

words.ex: Traditionally, people eat rice on New Year's Day.
words.ex_cn: 传统上，人们在新年那天吃米饭。
words.en: If something is done traditionally, it is done in a way that has been the custom for a long time.

words.ex: The factory is contaminating the river with its waste.
words.ex_cn: v. 工厂的废物正在污染河流。
words.en: To make something impure or unclean by contact or mixture with something unclean, bad, etc.

words.tr: n. 认识的人；熟人；“acquaintance”的复数
words.ex: He talks to his acquaintances every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每个周末都和熟人聊天。
words.en: People whom one knows but who are not particularly close friends.

words.ex: The artist added embellishments to the painting to make it more vibrant.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家在画作上添加了装饰，使其更加生动。
words.en: An embellishment is a detail added to something to make it more attractive or interesting.

words.tr: adv. 不知疲倦地，坚持不懈地
words.ex: She worked indefatigably to meet the project deadline.
words.ex_cn: 她不知疲倦地工作以赶上项目的截止日期。
words.en: In a way that shows tireless determination and unflagging energy.

words.ex: He ran energetically across the field.
words.ex_cn: 他精力充沛地跑过田野。
words.en: In a manner that shows or involves great activity or vitality.

words.tr: v. 使系统化；使有条理
words.ex: She is systematising the company's filing process.
words.ex_cn: 她正在使公司的文件归档过程系统化。
words.en: To arrange or organize something according to a system or method.

words.ex: He unequivocally denied the accusation.
words.ex_cn: 他明确否认了这项指控。
words.en: In a way that leaves no doubt; clearly and unambiguously.

words.ex: The services are provided contractually by the company.
words.ex_cn: 这些服务是由公司按照合同提供的。
words.en: In a way that is agreed in a contract.

words.ex: The ceremony was a glorification of the hero's achievements.
words.ex_cn: 这个仪式是对英雄成就的赞颂。
words.en: The act of describing or representing something as admirable, especially unjustifiably.

words.tr: v. 使标准化；使符合标准
words.ex: The company is standardising its production process to improve efficiency.
words.ex_cn: 公司正在标准化其生产过程以提高效率。
words.en: To make something conform to a standard; to establish a standard for something.

words.ex: The word 'this' is a determinative in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 在句子中，'this' 是一个限定词。
words.en: Serving to define, qualify, or direct.

words.ex: The city is overpopulated, leading to a shortage of resources.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市人口过多，导致资源短缺。
words.en: An area or place that is overpopulated has too many people living in it.

words.ex: He dressed appropriately for the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着得体地去参加了面试。
words.en: In a way that is suitable or proper in the circumstances.

words.tr: v. 取消，撤回（命令、订单等）
words.ex: The general countermanded the order to attack.
words.ex_cn: 将军取消了进攻的命令。
words.en: To revoke or cancel a previously issued order or command.

words.tr: v. 恶化；变坏；退化；“deteriorate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The weather is deteriorating quickly.
words.ex_cn: 天气正在迅速恶化。
words.en: Becoming progressively worse.

words.ex: The dust formed an agglomeration on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 灰尘在地板上形成了结块。
words.en: An agglomeration is a mass or collection of things; especially a cluster of disparate elements.

words.tr: adv. 不显眼地；不容易看到地；客气地
words.ex: She blended unobtrusively into the background.
words.ex_cn: 她不显眼地融入了背景中。
words.en: In a way that is not conspicuous or attracting attention.

words.tr: adj. 局限的；受限制的； v. “circumscribe”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: His ideas are circumscribed by tradition.
words.ex_cn: 他的想法受到传统的局限。
words.en: If someone's power or freedom is circumscribed, it is limited or restricted.

words.tr: n. 可能发生的事；不测事件
words.ex: We must prepare for all eventualities before starting the project.
words.ex_cn: 在开始项目之前，我们必须为所有可能发生的事做好准备。
words.en: Eventualities refer to possible events or outcomes, especially those that are uncertain or unforeseen.

words.ex: She looked at him reproachfully for his careless behavior.
words.ex_cn: 她责备地看着他，因为他的粗心行为。
words.en: In a manner that expresses disapproval or disappointment.

words.ex: He waits for the gratification of winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他等待赢得比赛的满足感。
words.en: Gratification is the pleasure or satisfaction you feel when you get something you wanted or worked for.

words.tr: adj. 纯粹的; 没有搀杂的
words.ex: She drank the unadulterated truth from the cup of his eyes.
words.ex_cn: 她从他眼睛的杯中饮下了纯粹的真相。
words.en: If you describe something as unadulterated, you mean that it is completely pure and has not been mixed with other things.

words.ex: The king's assassination shocked the whole country.
words.ex_cn: 国王的暗杀震惊了整个国家。
words.en: The act of killing someone important or famous, often for political reasons.

words.tr: v. 详细说明；特别指出
words.ex: The lawyer asked the witness to particularise the events of that day.
words.ex_cn: 律师要求证人详细说明那天的事件。
words.en: To particularise means to describe or explain something in detail, especially by giving specific examples or details.

words.ex: The constructions along the river are very old.
words.ex_cn: 河边的建筑物非常古老。
words.en: The act or process of building or constructing something; the way in which something is built or put together.

words.ex: The inviolability of human rights is important.
words.ex_cn: 人权的不可侵犯性很重要。
words.en: The quality of being immune to violation or intrusion; inviolable.

words.tr: adj. 从属的，下级的；v. 使从属，使服从
words.ex: The subordinating clause provides additional information about the main clause.
words.ex_cn: 从属从句提供了关于主句的额外信息。
words.en: Subordinating is the act of making something or someone less important than something or someone else, or the act of placing something in a lower or less important position.

words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件持客观态度。
words.en: If someone is disinterested in something, they have no personal involvement or investment in it and are therefore able to judge it fairly.

words.ex: My granddaughter loves to paint pictures.
words.ex_cn: 我的外孙女喜欢画画。
words.en: A granddaughter is the daughter of your son or daughter.

words.tr: n. 人工; 人造物; 不自然; 不自然之物
words.ex: The artificiality of the plastic flowers disappointed her.
words.ex_cn: 这些塑料花的人工感让她感到失望。
words.en: The quality of being artificial; something that is not natural or genuine.

words.tr: adj. 如百科辞典的，百科全书式的
words.ex: He has an encyclopaedic memory for facts.
words.ex_cn: 他对事实有着百科全书般的记忆力。
words.en: Comprehensive in terms of information or knowledge; resembling or characteristic of an encyclopedia.

words.tr: adv. 无可争辩地；无疑地
words.ex: The evidence was incontestably clear.
words.ex_cn: 证据无可争辩地清晰。
words.en: In a manner that is not able to be disputed or questioned.

words.tr: v. 使康复；使恢复名誉；修复
words.ex: After the surgery, he was rehabilitated through physical therapy.
words.ex_cn: 手术后，他通过物理治疗康复了。
words.en: To restore to a condition of health or useful and constructive activity.

words.tr: n. 经院哲学；墨守成规；尊重传统学风的思想
words.ex: He studied scholasticism in medieval philosophy class.
words.ex_cn: 他在中世纪哲学课上学习经院哲学。
words.en: A system of education and scholarship, especially in medieval Europe, emphasizing formal logic and authoritative texts.

words.tr: adv. 或者；作为一种选择；
words.ex: You can take the bus, or alternatively, walk to school.
words.ex_cn: 你可以坐公交车，或者 alternatively，走路去学校。
words.en: Used to introduce a suggestion that is different from the one already mentioned.

words.tr: n. 个人主义者，利己主义者
words.ex: He is an individualist who likes to make his own choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢自己做决定的个人主义者。
words.en: An individualist is a person who believes in the importance of individual freedom and self-reliance.

words.ex: The company's consolidation improved its market position.
words.ex_cn: 公司的巩固增强了其市场地位。
words.en: The act of combining two or more things into a single more effective or coherent whole.

words.ex: The car's accelerations were smooth and powerful.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的加速平稳而有力。
words.en: Accelerations refer to the process of increasing speed or the rate at which something happens or develops.

words.tr:
adj. 乐于助人的；随和的
v. 为某人提供住宿；容纳；适应；“accommodate”的现在分词
words.ex: He is always accommodating to his friends' needs.
words.ex_cn: 他总是满足朋友的需求。
words.en: If you describe someone as accommodating, you like the fact that they are willing to do things in order to please you or help you.

words.ex: The project is materialising into a successful venture.
words.ex_cn: v. 这个项目正在变成一个成功的冒险。
words.en: To materialise means to become actual fact; to happen or to make something happen.

words.ex: Statisticians analyze data to help companies make informed decisions.
words.ex_cn: 统计学家分析数据以帮助公司做出明智的决策。
words.en: Statisticians are professionals who collect, analyze, interpret, and present data to help solve real-world problems.

words.ex: The uncleanliness of the kitchen was appalling.
words.ex_cn: 厨房的肮脏程度令人震惊。
words.en: The state of being dirty or not clean.

words.tr: v. 使分解；使碎裂；使瓦解
words.ex: The old building disintegrates over time due to neglect.
words.ex_cn: v. 由于疏忽，这座老建筑随着时间的推移逐渐瓦解。
words.en: To break or decompose into parts or elements; to cause to lose cohesion or unity.

words.ex: He gave a philosophical answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个哲学性的回答。
words.en: Relating to or based on philosophy; calm and thoughtful in the face of problems.

words.tr: n. 共和主义；共和政体
words.ex: He supports republicanism in his country.
words.ex_cn: 他支持自己国家的共和主义。
words.en: Republicanism is a political ideology centered on citizenship in a state organized as a republic under which the people hold popular sovereignty.

words.ex: Each child has different personalities.
words.ex_cn: 每个孩子都有不同的人格。
words.en: The distinctive characteristics or qualities of a person, especially those that make them socially attractive.

words.tr: adj. 陈腐的；陈词滥调式的
words.ex: His speech was platitudinous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲陈词滥调，令人厌烦。
words.en: If you describe something said or written as platitudinous, you mean that it is dull and boring because it contains very obvious and simple ideas that have been repeated many times before.

words.tr:
adj. 领取退休金而退休的；过时的
v. 因年老而辞退；给养老金使…退休；“superannuate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The superannuated teacher still works part-time.
words.ex_cn: 这位退休的老师仍然兼职工作。
words.en: Too old to be effective or useful, especially in the context of employment.

words.tr: n. 技艺；手艺；精工细作
words.ex: The craftsmanship of the wooden chair is amazing.
words.ex_cn: 这把木椅的工艺非常出色。
words.en: The skill involved in making things by hand.

words.tr: n. 多余物；过剩；奢侈品
words.ex: The room was cluttered with superfluities that served no practical purpose.
words.ex_cn: 房间里堆满了没有实际用途的多余物品。
words.en: Superfluities refer to things that are not necessary or are more than what is needed, often implying excess or luxury.

words.ex: The government is dispossessing farmers of their land.
words.ex_cn: 政府正在剥夺农民的土地。
words.en: To dispossess someone of something means to take it away from them, especially when they have a right to it.

words.ex: The car stopped at the intersections.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在十字路口停了下来。
words.en: An intersection is a place where two or more roads cross each other.

words.tr: n. 插入；篡改；填写；插值
words.ex: The book has been criticized for numerous interpolations.
words.ex_cn: 这本书因多次篡改而受到批评。
words.en: Interpolation is the process of estimating unknown values that fall between known values.

words.tr: n. 结构；布局；配置；外形
words.ex: The configuration of the computer is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 这台电脑的配置非常简单。
words.en: The arrangement of parts or elements in a particular form, figure, or combination.

words.tr: adj. 未分配的；未分布的
words.ex: The money remains undistributed.
words.ex_cn: 这笔钱仍未分配。
words.en: Not distributed or allocated to a particular person or group.

words.tr:
n. 地中海；
adj. 地中海的；
words.ex: He sailed across the Mediterranean last summer.
words.ex_cn: 他去年夏天横渡了地中海。
words.en: relating to the Mediterranean Sea or the countries around it

words.ex: The museum sells low-cost reproductions of famous paintings.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆出售著名画作的廉价再制造品。
words.en: Reproductions are copies of original works, especially works of art, or the process of making such copies. In biology, it refers to the production of offspring by a sexual or asexual process.

words.ex: The juxtaposition of the old and the new buildings created a striking contrast.
words.ex_cn: 新旧建筑的并置形成了鲜明的对比。
words.en: The act or an instance of placing two or more things side by side often to compare or contrast or to create an interesting effect.

words.ex: The police arrested the housebreakers last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚逮捕了那些入室盗窃者。
words.en: Housebreakers are people who illegally enter a building, especially a house, in order to steal something.

words.tr: adj. 不为别人着想的；不体谅别人的；
words.ex: He left the door open and didn't care about others.
words.ex_cn: 他让门敞着，一点也不为别人着想。
words.en: If you describe someone as inconsiderate, you are criticizing them because they do not take enough care over how their words or actions will affect other people.

words.ex: He is relinquishing his position as CEO.
words.ex_cn: 他正在放弃他的CEO职位。
words.en: To relinquish means to voluntarily cease to keep or claim; to give up.

words.ex: Her sensitiveness to criticism made it difficult for her to accept feedback.
words.ex_cn: 她对批评的敏感性使得她很难接受反馈。
words.en: The quality or condition of being sensitive; the capacity to respond to slight changes, signals, or influences.

words.tr: adj. 排字上的；印刷上的
words.ex: The typo was a typographical error.
words.ex_cn: 这个拼写错误是一个排版错误。
words.en: Relating to the arrangement, appearance, or style of printed matter.

words.ex: She was remonstrating with her son about his poor grades.
words.ex_cn: v. 她正在就他儿子的糟糕成绩进行规劝。
words.en: To remonstrate means to make a forcefully reproachful protest or to argue in protest or opposition.

words.ex: The company failed due to mismanagement.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司因管理不善而倒闭了。
words.en: The act or process of managing something badly or wrongly.

words.ex: The play had two intermissions, allowing the audience to stretch their legs.
words.ex_cn: n. 这部剧有两场幕间休息，让观众可以活动一下腿脚。
words.en: An intermission is a short break between the parts of a play, film, concert, or other performance.

words.tr: n. 不相关的事物；无关紧要的事物
words.ex: The speaker's irrelevancies made it hard to follow his main point.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者无关紧要的话让人很难抓住他的主要观点。
words.en: Things that are not relevant or important to the matter at hand.

words.ex: He asked for clarification about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他要求对规则进行澄清。
words.en: A clarification is a statement that makes something clear or easier to understand.

words.tr: v. 使合理化；为…找理由
words.ex: He spent the evening rationalising his decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他花了一晚上为辞职的决定找理由。
words.en: To rationalise means to make something seem reasonable or to justify it, often by providing logical reasons or explanations.

words.tr: adj. 未被代表的；未被代理的
words.ex: Many small businesses feel unrepresented in the government's economic policies.
words.ex_cn: 许多小企业感觉在政府的经济政策中没有得到代表。
words.en: Not having someone to speak or act on one's behalf; not represented.

words.tr: n. 无误；教皇永无谬误论
words.ex: The pope is believed in his infallibility by some Catholics.
words.ex_cn: 一些天主教徒相信教皇的无误性。
words.en: The quality of being incapable of making mistakes or being wrong.

words.ex: The king issued several proclamations to inform the public about the new laws.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了几项公告，向公众通报新法律。
words.en: Proclamations are official public announcements or declarations, often made by a person in authority.

words.ex: He had foreknowledge of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他事先知道会有风暴。
words.en: Knowledge of something before it happens or exists.

words.tr: n. 一系列相互关联的事，连结
words.ex: The story was a concatenation of several different tales.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是一系列不同故事的连结。
words.en: The act of linking things together in a series or chain.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.ex: The professor recapitulates the main points of the lecture at the end.
words.ex_cn: 教授在讲座结束时重述了主要观点。
words.en: To summarize or repeat the main points of something.

words.ex: The exclusiveness of the club makes it very desirable.
words.ex_cn: 这个俱乐部的排他性使它非常令人向往。
words.en: The state of being exclusive, especially in being restricted to the people or things specified.

words.ex: He put the handkerchiefs in his pocket.
words.ex_cn: 他把手帕放进了口袋。
words.en: A handkerchief is a small square piece of fabric which you use for blowing your nose or wiping your face.

words.ex: The cities are geographically far apart.
words.ex_cn: 这些城市在地理上相距很远。
words.en: In terms of geography or physical location.

words.ex: The government is taking steps to prevent the monopolization of the market.
words.ex_cn: 政府正在采取措施防止市场垄断。
words.en: The act or process by which a person, group, or company comes to own or control all or nearly all of a particular market or resource, thereby excluding competition.

words.ex: He reads encyclopaedias to learn about animals and plants.
words.ex_cn: 他读百科全书来了解动植物。
words.en: A book or set of books giving information on many subjects or on many aspects of one subject and typically arranged alphabetically.

words.tr: adj. 不足取的；不值得考虑的；琐屑的
words.ex: The cost was inconsiderable.
words.ex_cn: 这个费用微不足道。
words.en: If you describe something as inconsiderable, you mean that it is small in amount or importance and not worth considering.

words.ex: The concept of transmigration is central to many Eastern religions.
words.ex_cn: n. 转世的概念在许多东方宗教中占据核心地位。
words.en: The movement of a soul from one body to another after death, a belief held by some religions.

words.ex: Many people joined the demonstrations for better wages.
words.ex_cn: 许多人参加了为争取更好工资的游行。
words.en: A demonstration is a march or gathering which people take part in to show their opposition to something or their support for something.

words.ex: The disarrangement of the files made it difficult to find the necessary documents.
words.ex_cn: 文件的混乱使得找到必要的文件变得困难。
words.en: The state of being disordered or untidy; a lack of order or arrangement.

words.ex: The country's economy showed signs of retrogressions after the political crisis.
words.ex_cn: 政治危机后，该国的经济显示出倒退的迹象。
words.en: The act or process of returning to an earlier and usually worse or less developed state.

words.ex: The program joins words by concatenations to make a sentence.
words.ex_cn: 这个程序通过连接词来组成句子。
words.en: The act of linking things together in a series or chain.

words.tr: n. 异族通婚；不同群体间的婚姻
words.ex: Intermarriages between different ethnic groups have become more common in recent years.
words.ex_cn: 近年来，不同种族群体之间的通婚变得更加普遍。
words.en: Marriages between members of different groups, especially different racial, ethnic, or religious groups.

words.tr: n. 对置，对换；逻辑中的对换命题
words.ex: In logic, contraposition is a type of immediate inference.
words.ex_cn: 在逻辑学中，对换是一种直接推理。
words.en: Contraposition is a logical relationship between two propositions, or statements. It is a type of immediate inference where the subject and predicate of a proposition are interchanged and negated.

words.ex: He uses many colloquialisms when talking with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时用很多口语表达。
words.en: A colloquialism is a word or phrase that is used in ordinary or familiar conversation but not in formal speech or writing.

words.ex: The two friends reached reconciliation after talking for hours.
words.ex_cn: 两个朋友经过几个小时的交谈后和好了。
words.en: Reconciliation is the process of making two opposite beliefs, ideas, or situations agree.

words.ex: The concept of metempsychosis is central to many Eastern religions.
words.ex_cn: 轮回的概念是许多东方宗教的核心。
words.en: The transmigration of the soul, especially its reincarnation after death.

words.ex: The meteorological report says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 气象报告说明天会下雨。
words.en: Relating to the branch of science concerned with the processes and phenomena of the atmosphere, especially as a means of forecasting the weather.

words.ex: The dress was covered in intricate embellishments.
words.ex_cn: 这件连衣裙上布满了复杂的装饰。
words.en: Embellishments are decorative details or features added to something to make it more attractive or interesting.

words.ex: The weather forecast predicts heavy precipitations tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预报预测明天会有大量降水。
words.en: Precipitations refer to the process of a substance being separated from a solution as a solid or the fall of water, ice, or snow from the atmosphere to the ground.

words.tr: adv. 轻松愉快地，无忧无虑地
words.ex: She laughed lightheartedly at the funny joke.
words.ex_cn: 她对这个有趣的笑话轻松地笑了。
words.en: In a cheerful and carefree manner.

words.ex: He can discriminating between real and fake coins.
words.ex_cn: 他能区分真币和假币。
words.en: If you describe someone as discriminating, you mean that they are able to recognize and appreciate the good qualities of something, especially things that are of high quality.

words.ex: The company wants centralization for better control.
words.ex_cn: 公司希望集中管理以更好地控制。
words.en: The process or policy of concentrating control of an organization or activity under a single authority.

words.tr: adj. （基督教）教会的；传教士的
words.ex: He wears an ecclesiastical robe.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着一件教会的长袍。
words.en: Relating to the Christian Church or its clergy.

words.ex: The government plans redistribution of wealth to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 政府计划重新分配财富以帮助穷人。
words.en: The act of distributing something again or differently, especially wealth or resources.

words.ex: The soil shows clear stratification in layers.
words.ex_cn: 土壤呈现出明显的分层。
words.en: The process or state of being divided into strata or layers, especially in society or geology.

words.ex: The handwriting was so messy that it was unrecognisable.
words.ex_cn: 字迹太乱，无法辨认。
words.en: not able to be recognized or identified

words.ex: She arrived inconveniently late for the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 她开会迟到了，很不方便。
words.en: In a manner that causes trouble or difficulty; not conveniently.

words.ex: He showed his qualifications for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他展示了自己胜任这份工作的资格。
words.en: The skills, qualities, or experience that you need in order to do something.

words.ex: The two friends have good understandings of each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两个朋友彼此之间有很好的理解。
words.en: An understanding is a mutual agreement or comprehension between people or groups.

words.ex: He looked at her contemptuously and turned away.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看了她一眼，然后转身走了。
words.en: In a manner showing contempt or disdain; scornfully.

words.ex: The data was analyzed arithmetically to ensure accuracy.
words.ex_cn: 数据被算术地分析以确保准确性。
words.en: In a manner relating to arithmetic.

words.ex: The news spread misinformation about the event.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻传播了关于该事件的错误信息。
words.en: Misinformation is false or inaccurate information, especially that which is deliberately intended to deceive.

words.tr: adj. 违背良心的；无节制的；过度的
words.ex: The prices they were charging were unconscionable.
words.ex_cn: 他们收取的价格是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe something as unconscionable, you mean that it is morally unacceptable, often because it is too large, too extreme, or too severe.

words.ex: The sophistication of the machine allows it to work very precisely.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的精密使其能够非常精确地工作。
words.en: Sophistication refers to the quality of being sophisticated, which includes complexity, refinement, and worldly experience.

words.ex: The correspondents reported live from the scene of the event.
words.ex_cn: 记者们从事件现场进行了现场报道。
words.en: A correspondent is a journalist who reports on news from a particular place or on a particular subject.

words.ex: The concentrations of salt in the water are too high.
words.ex_cn: 水中的盐浓度太高了。
words.en: The amount of a particular substance within a solution or in a particular volume of space.

words.tr: n. 英担（英国重量单位，等于112磅或50.8公斤）
words.ex: The shipment weighed several hundredweights.
words.ex_cn: 这批货物重达几英担。
words.en: A unit of weight equal to 112 pounds or 50.8 kilograms, used in the UK.

words.tr: adj. 位于上方的；压在…上面的
words.ex: The superincumbent layers of rock were carefully removed to reveal the fossil.
words.ex_cn: 位于上方的岩石层被小心地移开，以露出化石。
words.en: Situated or lying above something else; overlying.

words.tr: v. 分散；分权；去中心化
words.ex: The company is decentralising its operations to improve efficiency.
words.ex_cn: v. 公司正在分散其运营以提高效率。
words.en: To decentralise means to distribute the administrative functions or powers of (a central authority) over a less concentrated area.

words.tr: v. 故意对…作错误的报道( misrepresent的过去式和过去分词 )
words.ex: He misrepresented the facts to the judge.
words.ex_cn: 他向法官歪曲了事实。
words.en: To give a false or misleading account of the nature of something.

words.ex: The church follows a congregational governance model.
words.ex_cn: 该教堂遵循会众治理模式。
words.en: Relating to a congregation, especially a church congregation.

words.tr: v. 使彻底变革( revolutionize的过去式和过去分词 )
words.ex: The smartphone revolutionized the way people communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机彻底改变了人们的交流方式。
words.en: To completely change something so that it is much better.

words.ex: The miscalculation of the budget led to a financial crisis.
words.ex_cn: 预算的误算导致了金融危机。
words.en: An incorrect calculation or estimate.

words.ex: The teacher drew several parallelograms on the board to explain the concept of opposite sides being equal.
words.ex_cn: 老师在黑板上画了几个平行四边形来解释对边相等的概念。
words.en: A parallelogram is a four-sided plane rectilinear figure with opposite sides parallel.

words.ex: He provided several justifications for his actions.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的行为提供了几个正当理由。
words.en: Reasons or arguments given to defend or explain an action, belief, or decision.

words.ex: The implementation of the new rule took one month.
words.ex_cn: 新规则的履行花了一个月。
words.en: The act of putting a decision or plan into effect; execution.

words.ex: The aggrandisement of his wealth was evident after the successful business deal.
words.ex_cn: n. 他财富的增加在成功的商业交易后显而易见。
words.en: The act of increasing the power, status, or wealth of someone or something.

words.ex: Protectionists argue that tariffs are necessary to safeguard domestic industries.
words.ex_cn: 保护主义者认为关税是保护国内工业的必要手段。
words.en: Protectionists are people who advocate for the protection of domestic industries through tariffs and other trade barriers.

words.tr: v. 重新合并；重新并入
words.ex: The company reincorporated in Delaware to take advantage of the state's business-friendly laws.
words.ex_cn: v. 公司重新在特拉华州注册，以利用该州对商业友好的法律。
words.en: To form a new corporation or to include something again in a larger entity.

words.ex: The city is known for its large agglomerations of people during festivals.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市以节日期间大量人群的聚集而闻名。
words.en: An agglomeration is a mass or collection of things that have come together.

words.ex: His peregrinations took him to many exotic locations.
words.ex_cn: 他的旅行带他去了许多异国情调的地方。
words.en: Peregrinations refer to travels or wanderings, especially those that are extensive or meandering.

words.tr: adj. 难接近的；不友好的；冷漠的
words.ex: The old man was unapproachable and never smiled.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人难以接近，从不微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as unapproachable, you mean that they seem unfriendly and not easy to talk to.

words.ex: The gratifications of a job well done are immense.
words.ex_cn: 完成一项工作后的满足感是巨大的。
words.en: Gratifications refer to the pleasures or satisfactions that one gets from something.

words.tr: v. 开除教籍；逐出教会
words.ex: He was excommunicated for his heretical views.
words.ex_cn: 他因异端观点被开除教籍。
words.en: To officially exclude someone from participation in the sacraments and services of the Christian Church.

words.tr: n. 预定，预言; 天数; 天缘
words.ex: The concept of predestination is central to many religions.
words.ex_cn: 预定论是许多宗教的核心概念。
words.en: The belief that everything that happens has already been decided by God or fate and cannot be changed.

words.ex: He cried because of the sentimentality of the old movie.
words.ex_cn: 他因为那部老电影的感伤而哭了。
words.en: Sentimentality is the quality of being sentimental, especially in a way that seems exaggerated or foolish.

words.ex: The meeting was filled with unpleasantness.
words.ex_cn: 会议充满了不愉快。
words.en: The state or quality of being unpleasant; something that is unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 依照环境的；间接的；详细的
words.ex: He gave a circumstantial explanation based on the situation.
words.ex_cn: 他根据情况给出了一个依照环境的解释。
words.en: Circumstantial evidence is evidence that suggests something by implication rather than direct proof.

words.ex: His expostulations fell on deaf ears as the committee proceeded with their plan.
words.ex_cn: 他的劝诫被置若罔闻，委员会继续执行他们的计划。
words.en: Expostulations are strong expressions of disagreement or disapproval, often in the form of protests or remonstrances.

words.ex: The rectifications made to the document improved its accuracy.
words.ex_cn: 对文件进行的修正提高了其准确性。
words.en: The act of correcting or adjusting something to make it right or accurate.

words.ex: He made a generalization from the data.
words.ex_cn: 他从数据中做出了一个概括。
words.en: A generalization is a statement that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

words.tr: adv. 铺张地，招摇地，炫耀地
words.ex: She dressed ostentatiously for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为聚会盛装打扮。
words.en: In a way that is characterized by vulgar or pretentious display; designed to impress or attract notice.

words.tr: adj. 无法确定的；无法解决的
words.ex: The exact cause of the problem is indeterminable.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的确切原因无法确定。
words.en: If something is indeterminable, it cannot be determined or decided.

words.ex: The village is underpopulated and quiet.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄人口稀少，很安静。
words.en: An area that is underpopulated has too few people living in it.

words.ex: He is superintending the construction site.
words.ex_cn: 他正在监督建筑工地。
words.en: To oversee or manage a project, organization, or activity.

words.ex: Hypothetically, if you study hard, you will pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 假设你努力学习，你就会通过考试。
words.en: In a way that involves or is based on a hypothesis; as a hypothesis.

words.tr: v. 预先决定；预先确定
words.ex: He is predetermining the outcome before the game starts.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛开始前就预定了结果。
words.en: To decide or establish something in advance.

words.ex: The misapplication of funds led to the project's failure.
words.ex_cn: 资金的滥用导致了项目的失败。
words.en: The incorrect or improper use of something.

words.ex: He breathes intermittently during sleep.
words.ex_cn: 他在睡觉时呼吸间歇地。
words.en: If something happens intermittently, it happens at irregular intervals, not continuously.

words.tr: n. 返老还童；恢复青春
words.ex: The rejuvenescence of the old tree surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树的复苏让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The process of becoming young or youthful again; the restoration of youthful vigor or appearance.

words.tr: n. 可转移性；可转让性
words.ex: The transferability of his skills helps him find new jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他技能的可转移性帮助他找到新工作。
words.en: The quality of being able to be transferred or moved from one place, person, or situation to another.

words.ex: He faced many discouragements but kept trying.
words.ex_cn: 他遇到了很多挫折，但仍然坚持尝试。
words.en: The feeling of despair in the face of obstacles or setbacks.

words.tr: n. 成就；成绩；造诣；完成( accomplishment的名词复数 )；
words.ex: His accomplishments include winning three gold medals.
words.ex_cn: 他的成就包括赢得三枚金牌。
words.en: Achievements or successes in a particular area.

words.tr: n. 解放；选举权的授予
words.ex: The enfranchisement of women gave them the right to vote.
words.ex_cn: 妇女的解放赋予了她们投票权。
words.en: Enfranchisement refers to the granting of the right to vote or the act of freeing someone from legal, social, or political restrictions.

words.tr:
adj. 有全权的
n. 全权代表
words.ex: The plenipotentiary was given authority to negotiate the treaty.
words.ex_cn: 全权代表被赋予了谈判条约的权力。
words.en: A plenipotentiary is a person, especially a diplomat, who is given full powers by their government to make decisions or take action on their behalf.

words.tr: n．; 1. 管理，行政：对组织、企业或国家的管理和运作。; 2. 政府，政府当局：特指国家或地区的...
words.ex: The city had five administrations in ten years.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市在十年内换了五届政府。
words.en: The act or process of administering, especially the management of a government or large institution.

words.ex: He said he lost his job, euphemistically, he was fired.
words.ex_cn: 他委婉地说自己丢了工作，其实就是被解雇了。
words.en: In a way that uses a mild or indirect word or expression instead of one considered to be harsh, blunt, or offensive.

words.tr: n. 不满；令人不满的事物；
words.ex: He showed dissatisfaction with the new rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定表示不满。
words.en: Dissatisfaction is a feeling of not being satisfied or pleased with something.

words.ex: The workers leave the slaughterhouses at six p.m.
words.ex_cn: 工人们晚上六点离开屠宰场。
words.en: A slaughterhouse is a place where animals are killed for their meat.

words.tr: adv. 非故意地；无意之中；
words.ex: He unintentionally broke the vase.
words.ex_cn: 他非故意地打碎了花瓶。
words.en: If you do something unintentionally, you do it without intending to do it.

words.tr: v. 互相连接，互相联系( interconnect的现在分词)
words.ex: The wires are interconnecting the devices.
words.ex_cn: 这些电线正在连接这些设备。
words.en: To connect with each other.

words.tr: n. 不服从；不顺从；反抗
words.ex: The sergeant punished the soldier for insubordination.
words.ex_cn: 中士因不服从而惩罚了士兵。
words.en: Insubordination is the act of deliberately not obeying someone in authority.

words.tr: n. 复杂性；精密性；世故
words.ex: The phone has many new sophistications.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有许多新的复杂功能。
words.en: The quality of being sophisticated, especially in terms of complexity, refinement, or worldly experience.

words.ex: He works in a nonagricultural job in the city.
words.ex_cn: 他在城市里从事一份非农业的工作。
words.en: Not related to agriculture or farming.

words.tr: n. 不可能的事；不可能性
words.ex: He faced many impossibilities but never gave up.
words.ex_cn: 他面对了许多不可能的事情，但从不放弃。
words.en: Things that cannot be done or achieved; the state or condition of being impossible.

words.ex: The electromagnetic wave travels through space.
words.ex_cn: 电磁波在太空中传播。
words.en: Relating to the interrelation of electric currents or fields and magnetic fields.

words.ex: Philanthropists give money to help poor children.
words.ex_cn: 慈善家们捐钱帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: A philanthropist is a person who seeks to promote the welfare of others, especially by the generous donation of money to good causes.

words.ex: The doctor studied epidemiological data to find the cause of the disease.
words.ex_cn: 医生研究了流行病学数据以找出疾病的原因。
words.en: Relating to the branch of medicine which deals with the incidence, distribution, and possible control of diseases and other factors relating to health.

words.tr: adv. 作为插入语地；顺便地说
words.ex: He said, parenthetically, that he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他顺便说了一下，他很累。
words.en: In a manner that is incidental or digressive, often used to introduce additional information into a sentence.

words.tr: n. 减产；生产不足；生产供不应求
words.ex: The factory has underproduction this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个工厂这个月产量不足。
words.en: The production of less of a commodity or product than is needed or expected.

words.ex: His argument is based on false presuppositions.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点基于错误的假设。
words.en: A presupposition is something that you assume to be true, especially something which you must assume is true in order to continue with a line of argument or a course of action.

words.ex: The teacher gave different interpretations of the poem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这首诗给出了不同的解释。
words.en: The act of explaining or making clear the meaning of something.

words.tr: n. 不可调和的人或事物
words.ex: They are irreconcilables and will never agree.
words.ex_cn: 他们是无法调和的，永远不会达成一致。
words.en: People or things that cannot be reconciled or made to agree.

words.ex: The movie shows the objectification of women.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了对女性的物化。
words.en: The act of treating a person as a mere object, disregarding their personality or dignity.

words.tr: adv. 按时间的前后顺序排列地
words.ex: He listed the events chronologically.
words.ex_cn: 他按时间顺序列出了这些事件。
words.en: In a manner that follows the order in which events occurred.

words.tr: v. 区分，区别，辨别；区别； adj. [计] 微分的 v. 区分，区别，辨别( differentiate的现在分词 )；
words.ex: He is differentiating between the two similar words.
words.ex_cn: 他正在区分这两个相似的词。
words.en: To differentiate means to recognize or express the difference between things or people.

words.ex: The disorganisation of the team caused many delays.
words.ex_cn: 团队的无组织导致了许多延误。
words.en: Disorganisation refers to a lack of order or organisation, often leading to confusion or inefficiency.

words.ex: The new rule counterbalances the advantage of the stronger team.
words.ex_cn: 新规则抵消了较强队伍的优势。
words.en: To counterbalance something means to have an equal and opposite effect on it, so that it does not have too much of a particular quality or effect.

words.tr: adj. 不符合议会惯例的；不礼貌的
words.ex: His remark was unparliamentary and shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的言论是不恰当的，让所有人都震惊了。
words.en: Not in accordance with parliamentary rules or etiquette; impolite or rude in a parliamentary context.

words.ex: He listened sympathetically to her story.
words.ex_cn: 他同情地听她讲了自己的故事。
words.en: In a way that shows you understand and care about someone's suffering or problems.

words.tr: adj. 不容置疑的；无可否认的
words.ex: The evidence is incontrovertible.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If something is incontrovertible, it is definitely true and cannot be disputed.

words.ex: The punishment was disproportionate to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 惩罚与罪行不成比例。
words.en: Something that is disproportionate is surprisingly large or small in comparison to something else.

words.tr: adj. 不能熄灭的；不能扑灭的；不能消灭的
words.ex: His love for her was inextinguishable.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的爱是无法熄灭的。
words.en: If a feeling or quality is inextinguishable, it is so strong that it cannot be destroyed or ended.

words.tr: v. 不赞成；不支持；使难堪
words.ex: He is discountenancing cheating in class.
words.ex_cn: 他正在反对课堂上的作弊行为。
words.en: To discountenance means to disapprove of or discourage something, often by showing disapproval or making someone feel embarrassed.

words.ex: He is counterbalancing the weight with a stone.
words.ex_cn: 他用一块石头来平衡重量。
words.en: To counterbalance something means to have an equal and opposite effect to it, so that it does not have too much influence or importance.

words.tr: n. 不可兑换性；不能转换性
words.ex: The inconvertibility of the currency caused problems.
words.ex_cn: 货币的不可兑换性引起了问题。
words.en: The state of being unable to be converted or exchanged into another form, especially currency.

words.tr: adj. 违背宪法的；违反宪章（或章程）的
words.ex: The law is unconstitutional because it violates basic rights.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律是违宪的，因为它侵犯了基本权利。
words.en: If something is unconstitutional, it is against the constitution of a particular country or organization.

words.ex: The commensurability of the two projects was evident in their shared goals.
words.ex_cn: 这两个项目的可公度性在他们共同的目标中显而易见。
words.en: The quality of being measurable by the same standard; comparability.

words.ex: He shows conscientiousness in doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他在做作业时表现出认真负责。
words.en: The quality of being careful and thorough in one's work or duties.

words.ex: The two twins are indistinguishable in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 照片中的这对双胞胎难以区分。
words.en: If one thing is indistinguishable from another, the two things are so similar that it is difficult to know which is which or to tell them apart.

words.tr: n. 意见不一；误解( misunderstanding的名词复数 )；
words.ex: Their misunderstandings caused a big argument.
words.ex_cn: 他们的意见不一导致了一场大争吵。
words.en: A misunderstanding is a failure to understand something correctly, often leading to confusion or disagreement.
